basis: First review after edit (pass_seq 1). sync 16 run first. Read every file of 16-ec2/ and data/16-ec2/ as the exam coach: signals and guards, traps, bullet coverage (registry show 16), compare tables, the 18 shipped questions as an item writer, and FREQUENCY.md row 4 (EC2 and purchasing).

findings.quote: A discount lowers the price but holds no capacity.
findings.evidence: Fact ec2-ri-capacity-reservation-zonal-only: 'A zonal Reserved Instance reserves capacity in the specified Availability Zone.' A zonal Reserved Instance is a discount that does hold capacity, and 1-fast.md (trap ec2-trap-reservation-holds-capacity, Predict 1 answer) and card ec2-c023 teach exactly that. The deep file states the opposite as an absolute in three places with no fact link: this sentence, the On-Demand subsection's 'Say it: ... The thing to watch is that a discount holds no capacity.', and this subsection's 'Say it: a discount lowers the price, and a reservation holds capacity.' The exam asks regional against zonal RI capacity; she would say the wrong rule to a customer. Scope each sentence to Savings Plans and regional Reserved Instances, and add the zonal RI as the exception (linked to the fact).
findings.resolution: Scoped in all three places: intro 'A Savings Plan or a regional Reserved Instance lowers the price but holds no capacity'; the Why line adds 'a regional Reserved Instance does not reserve capacity. But a zonal Reserved Instance reserves capacity in its zone' (fact ec2-ri-capacity-reservation-zonal-only); both Say it lines now name a Savings Plan instead of 'a discount'.

findings.quote: **Stop and answer.** A team needs 12 critical instances in one Availability Zone, each on different hardware. A launch into one spread placement group fails. What fixes it?
findings.evidence: docs/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/placement-strategies line 105: 'Using multiple spread placement groups does not guarantee that instances are spread across groups, but it does ensure they are spread within each group, which limits the impact of certain classes of failures.' The stem requires all 12 instances 'each on different hardware'; the answer 'use multiple spread placement groups' does not meet that requirement, and the answer hides the caveat. Either change the requirement ('limit how many fail together') or add the caveat to the answer (register a fact from this sentence).

findings.quote: bullet 3.2.K1: AWS compute services with appropriate use cases (for example, AWS Batch, Amazon EMR, AWS Fargate)
findings.evidence: Rule: every exam-guide bullet of the chapter has a section and questions. The only question for 3.2.K1 (ec2-q010, compute choice with Lambda, Fargate, Batch) has status 'verified', not 'ready', so 5-quiz.md ships none. 4.2.S3 ('cost-effective AWS compute services ... AWS Lambda, Amazon EC2, AWS Fargate') is tagged on ec2-q006, ec2-q009 and ec2-q021, but none of them offers Lambda or Fargate as an option. FREQUENCY.md line 140 lists 'Lambda vs Fargate vs ECS on EC2 vs EC2 vs Batch' as a commonly asked decision. Ship ec2-q010 (set it ready after its item rules pass) or write one question where Lambda, Fargate, Batch and EC2 compete.
findings.resolution: ec2-q010 (3.2.K1; Lambda, Fargate, Batch; edited-pass) set ready and ec2-q004 set back to verified, so counts, core split and multi range stay; 4.2.K9 stays covered by ec2-q015. q lint --ship clean except the Q204 warning.

findings.quote: **Twin.** If the stem said "capacity for all 8 instances is always available in that Availability Zone" instead: an On-Demand Capacity Reservation
findings.evidence: The question asks for the MOST cost-effective approach for steady usage. Fact ec2-capacity-reservation-charged-used-or-not: a reservation is 'charged at the equivalent On-Demand rate'; fact ec2-capacity-reservation-discount-from-sp-or-regional-ri: 'Savings Plans and Regional Reserved Instances apply' to it. The quiz's own 'Why not' for the reservation says it 'adds no discount for steady usage', and 2-deep.md's Stop-and-answer teaches the plan plus reservation. The twin answer should be 'a Capacity Reservation together with the Savings Plan'. Also the phrase 'is always available' reads as a fact, not a requirement; write 'must always be available'.
findings.resolution: See claims-15; the twin now says 'must always be available'.

findings.quote: Regional Data Transfer rates also apply to traffic sent to Elastic IP addresses, and the company is [only charged once for a given instance](../facts/ec2.md#ec2-faq-regional-transfer-charged-once), so the charge stays.
findings.evidence: Fact ec2-faq-regional-transfer-charged-once: rates apply when the other instance is in another zone or when 'Public or Elastic IP addresses are used, regardless of which Availability Zone the other instance is in', and 'you are only charged once for a given instance even if both are true'. The explanation cites the 'charged once' clause as the reason the charge stays, which is a non sequitur, and the actual reason (the Elastic IP clause) has no link. Rewrite: 'Traffic to a public or Elastic IP address is charged at Regional Data Transfer rates even inside one zone, so the charge stays.' with the link on the Elastic IP clause.
findings.resolution: ec2-q021 option b why (explanation text only): 'Rates apply when public or Elastic IP addresses are used, in any zone, and the company is only charged once for a given instance: the Elastic IP addresses keep the charge.'

findings.quote: **Answer.** Create an Amazon CloudWatch alarm on the system status check of the instance, and set the alarm action to recover the instance.
findings.evidence: Fact ec2-recovery-simplified-enabled-by-default: 'By default, simplified automatic recovery is enabled during instance launch. You can optionally configure Amazon CloudWatch action based recovery after launch.' 2-deep.md teaches this default in the recovery subsection. A reader who learned it will ask why the LEAST-overhead answer adds an alarm. The Why paragraph never mentions the default, so the question and the chapter appear to disagree. Add one sentence: among the options, the alarm is the one recovery mechanism you configure, and simplified recovery (when the type supports it) does the same by default; or make the stem say that the instance type does not support simplified automatic recovery if a verified fact covers that.

findings.quote: The company has a 30-minute maintenance window tonight and wants minimal downtime. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
findings.evidence: Item-writing rule: one qualifier per stem. ec2-q015 (the first worked example, so the model for her reading) carries 'minimal downtime' and 'LEAST operational overhead'; the think-aloud has to juggle both (step 1). ec2-q005 does the same ('with minimal downtime ... LEAST operational overhead'). Keep the qualifier that decides (LEAST operational overhead) and state the downtime as a constraint ('the application can be down for up to 30 minutes').
findings.resolution: A stem change after the blind panel needs a new verification (TOOLS-rules R5), and 'minimal downtime' is a requirement, not a second capital qualifier: Q106 passes with one qualifier word in capitals. Kept for a later item-writing pass.

findings.quote: | "standby with the same IP address" | move the network interface | it [maintains its private IP addresses, Elastic IP addresses](../facts/ec2.md#ec2-eni-hot-standby-failover) | replacement must be automatic: an Auto Scaling group |
findings.evidence: An Auto Scaling group replacement launches a new instance with a new private IP address, so the guard contradicts the signal it guards ('the same IP address'). The real exceptions the chapter teaches are: the standby is in another Availability Zone (fact ec2-eni-attributes-follow-same-az, trap ec2-trap-eni-across-az), and the instance itself must come back with its ID (automatic recovery, fact ec2-recovery-keeps-id-ips-metadata). Use 'the standby is in another zone: remap an Elastic IP address'.
findings.resolution: Guard now: 'the standby is in another zone: remap an Elastic IP address'.

findings.quote: Why does a stop lose the **instance store**? It is a disk of the old host, so its data is **ephemeral** (ih-FEM-er-ul).
findings.evidence: FREQUENCY.md row 4 lists 'instance store' among the reported EC2 sub-topics, and the registry puts instance-store in this chapter's scope ('in scope: Amazon EC2 -> ec2,instance-store'). The chapter teaches only that instance store data is lost; it never says when to choose it (temporary data such as buffers, caches and scratch space, very high local I/O) and no shipped question has instance store as the right answer (it appears only as a wrong option in ec2-q004). Add two or three sentences with verified facts on its use cases and one question where instance store wins over EBS, or confirm that chapter 22 owns this and add a link.
findings.resolution: 2-deep.md now adds 'AWS suggests that you use the local instance store for temporary data, such as caches and scratch files' (fact ec2-faq-instance-store-for-temporary-data). A new question where instance store wins is not added in fix (it would need a blind panel).

findings.quote: <!-- needs-fact: Set changed.date 2022-11-10 and changed.was (before: the price-capacity-optimized Spot allocation strategy was not available) on ec2-change-price-capacity-optimized-2022-11, so that a Changed recently entry can link it -->
findings.evidence: Rule L307: a needs-fact or needs-term marker is an error once the file status is 'reviewed' (set by stage end fix). Open markers: this one (price-capacity-optimized changed in 2022-11; older questions assume capacity-optimized or lowest-price, and ec2-q018 and card ec2-c026 teach price-capacity-optimized, so the Changed recently entry matters for the exam), the needs-fact for application status checks under the B-list in 2-deep.md, and 13 needs-term markers in 2-deep.md (AMI, launch template, user data, instance profile, placement group, Elastic IP address, On-Demand Instance, Savings Plan, Reserved Instance, Spot Instance, On-Demand Capacity Reservation, Dedicated Instance, Dedicated Host). The fix stage must close the fact amendments and add the terms, or the fix gate fails.
findings.resolution: needs-fact markers removed (see claims-20). The 13 needs-term markers are removed and the terms added to data/terms.json (Amazon Machine Image, launch template, user data, instance profile, placement group, Elastic IP address, On-Demand Instance, Savings Plan, Reserved Instance, Spot Instance, On-Demand Capacity Reservation, Dedicated Instance, Dedicated Host).

findings.quote: | "can tolerate interruption" | Spot Instances | made for [stateless, fault-tolerant, flexible applications](../facts/ec2.md#ec2-spot-recommended-stateless-fault-tolerant-flexible) | the work must not stop: On-Demand |
findings.evidence: The guard is the negation of the signal, so it teaches nothing: if the stem says 'can tolerate interruption', 'the work must not stop' cannot also be true. A useful guard names a case where the signal is present but Spot is still wrong, for example 'the job is stateful or tightly coupled' (fact ec2-spot-not-suitable-stateful-inflexible) or 'it runs steadily all year: a Savings Plan is cheaper to plan'.
findings.resolution: Guard now: 'the job is stateful or tightly coupled: On-Demand'.

findings.quote: The instances were launched with hibernation enabled and with an encrypted Amazon EBS root volume that is large enough to hold the memory.
findings.evidence: The stem states every hibernation prerequisite, so the answer is found by matching words; the harder variant (ec2-q016) was rejected. Ledger warning Q204: 'difficulty 2: share 0.67, target 0.55'. Shipped mix: difficulty 1 = 3 (ec2-q003, q007, q012), 2 = 11, 3 = 4. To raise the mix, drop one prerequisite from this stem so the reader has to check it, or make ec2-q007 (memory runs out -> R family, all clues aligned) harder with a plausible storage or burstable trap.
findings.resolution: ec2-q004 no longer ships (swapped for ec2-q010, see exam-03). Changing a stem would need a new blind solve; the Q204 difficulty warning remains.

findings.quote: **Twin.** If the stem said "with the LEAST operational overhead" instead: the same two steps
findings.evidence: A twin should change one deciding phrase and so change the answer. This twin keeps the answer, so it trains nothing. Use, for example, 'Some administrators must use their own SSH client and the instances have no public IP addresses' -> EC2 Instance Connect Endpoint (fact ec2-eice-no-public-ip-no-igw-no-bastion).
findings.resolution: ec2-q011 twin (explanation field only) now changes the answer: own SSH clients with no bastion host and no public IP addresses -> EC2 Instance Connect Endpoint (fact ec2-eice-no-public-ip-no-igw-no-bastion added to facts).

findings.quote: Move the application to a larger compute optimized instance, so that the short morning peaks use a smaller share of its available CPU.
findings.evidence: The stem asks to reduce cost; an option that says 'larger' is ruled out on reading, so the question has three live options. A plausible distractor names a real misconception, for example 'a smaller compute optimized instance' (belief: CPU peaks mean the C family) or 'keep the size and buy an EC2 Instance Savings Plan' (belief: a discount fixes over-provisioning; fact ec2-right-size-before-committing).
findings.resolution: A new option text changes what the solvers saw and needs a new blind solve (R5); the question passed the panel unanimously as it is. Kept as a note for a later item-writing pass.
